title: `ia validate` binds every `@check` and records the bound ones that passed or failed as runtime `@observation` evidence
summary: Plan amendments C14, C15, C22 and C23. @inventarch/db adds bindChecks(records, report, catalog), checkVerdicts(verdicts, runner, scope, excluded?), WHOLE_WORKSPACE_SCOPE ('*'), the CheckBinding, CheckBindingStatus, CheckCatalog and CheckOutcome types, EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY ('.ia/work/evidence'), EVIDENCE_FILE, CHECK_EVIDENCE_WORD, evidenceText, readEvidence, writeEvidence (with an optional pruneBefore) with the EvidenceObservation and EvidenceWrite types, InputOptions.evidence, InputSnapshot.evidence (candidates listed by path, size and modification time) and the EvidenceCandidate type. COMP-CHECK's pass for a check only structural admission admits counts as not-evaluated. A built-in evaluator is always bound, with the aggregate of the admission verdicts its text check.scope selects: every one for the documented whole-workspace token *, otherwise exactly the verdicts whose scope equals it; fail dominates, then not-evaluated, then pass, and an empty selection (a prose or unknown scope, or an evaluator that reported nothing) is not-evaluated, never a pass. Any other evaluator binds against the evaluators section of the catalog the workspace's host joined, through the same trust and joined catalog as execution bindings: unavailable without a catalog, when the catalog does not list it, lists it unavailable or is not valid, revoked (an error) when it revokes it or failed verification, and bound but never invoked, so not-evaluated, when it supports it, since no host implementation runs an evaluator in this release. A payload without a catalog, such as 2.0.0's, leaves every catalog check unavailable, never revoked. @inventarch/distribution adds WorkspaceSession.checks(trust) with the ValidationChecks type, SessionOptions with checks, WorkspaceSession.openedAt, WorkspaceAdmission.authoredRevision and recordValidation(session, checks), the one writer of evidence; WorkspaceSession.validation(), bindings() and checks() still read only, and a session never reads evidence, so what a validation admits, binds, counts and exits with is the authored view alone and its revision is the one every other reader reports, as in 2.0.0. Behavior change: ia validate and ia-distribution validate, until now read-only, write .ia/work/evidence/<authored revision>.ia whenever a bound check passed or failed: one `@observation` per such check, named <check name>-<12 hex authored revision>, verdict success or refusal, at runtime placement band 0, staged and renamed into place, the same bytes on a second validate at one authored revision, and the files of other authored revisions pruned best effort (a file the process may not remove, or one modified after the run read its inputs, is kept, and pruning never refuses); a not-evaluated check records nothing, a workspace without the `@observation` word records nothing, and a validation whose admission is refused records and prunes nothing; since a failing built-in verdict always refuses admission, ia validate never writes a refusal observation in this release. Evidence never moves the authored revision, the position packet, the host projection or what any other reader admits: only a reader opened with evidence reads the current authored revision's file, and only when its admission is not refused and the writer, binding that reader's own checks again and taking the times from the file itself, reproduces it byte for byte (so a forged verdict, reason, record or time, an observation for a check not evaluated, a relationship or any other byte is not evidence) and adding it changes nothing the authored records admit; db exports reproducesEvidence for that test. The writer keeps an observation's first times only from such a file; a time not in the writer's exact stamp, with observed and captured apart, or more than five minutes ahead of the reading clock is not evidence; any other time is carried as written, not verified. A current file found unchanged is touched, so a validation of another revision that began earlier never prunes it. Where this revision's evidence must be written and cannot be (a read-only checkout) both validations now refuse, before anything is pruned, ia validate with IA-DIST-EVIDENCE-UNWRITABLE at exit 3, and a link, junction or file at .ia/work or .ia/work/evidence refuses as IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE; nothing is ever read through one, and with nothing to record neither validation refuses for it; a CI job that validated a read-only tree with passing checks under 2.0.0 must make .ia/work writable. ia validate's human report adds a Checks section (the catalog source when a check needs one, one entry per check with its evaluator, binding, outcome and reason, and what was recorded) and summary lines for revoked and not-evaluated checks, and closes with a not-evaluated note when a check was not evaluated; --json adds checks and evidence, and ia-distribution validate adds both to its result; a revoked check exits 1. --json adds authoredRevision beside revision. ia doctor, ia capture --preview and refused effects never create or prune evidence. Limits: no evaluator runs, the host registers no evaluator codec, and only built-in evaluators produce evidence.
